title: Fairness Evaluation in Text Classification: Machine Learning Practitioner Perspectives of Individual and Group Fairness

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating group fairness via performance metrics (accuracy, false positive/negative rates) on text subgroups containing racial/ethnic identity terms, and evaluating individual fairness via counterfactual substitution of these terms in sentence templates.

Evaluating group fairness via performance metrics on text subgroups containing sexual orientation identity terms (e.g., gay, lesbian, bisexual), and evaluating individual fairness via counterfactual substitution of these terms.

Evaluating group fairness via performance metrics on text subgroups containing gender identity terms (e.g., transgender, nonbinary, male, female), and evaluating individual fairness via counterfactual substitution of these terms.

Evaluating group fairness via performance metrics on text subgroups containing religious identity terms (e.g., muslim, christian, jewish), and evaluating individual fairness via counterfactual substitution of these terms.

Evaluating group fairness via performance metrics on text subgroups containing disability-related identity terms (e.g., blind, deaf, paralyzed), and evaluating individual fairness via counterfactual substitution of these terms.

Evaluating group fairness via performance metrics on text subgroups containing age-related identity terms (e.g., elderly, young, millennial), and evaluating individual fairness via counterfactual substitution of these terms.

Evaluating group fairness via performance metrics on text subgroups containing nationality identity terms (e.g., american, canadian, european), and evaluating individual fairness via counterfactual substitution of these terms.
Evaluated during the exploration phase through custom user inputs comparing model performance and counterfactual sentence substitutions using political identity terms (e.g., democrat, communist).
Evaluated during the exploration phase through custom user inputs comparing model performance and counterfactual sentence substitutions using socioeconomic status terms (e.g., poor, lower-class).
